symbols.w: a weight: the strength of one connection; w_ji runs into unit j from unit i
symbols.i: counts inputs or weights; in w_ji, the unit the wire comes from
symbols.x: an input value arriving at a unit; x_ji is the signal on the wire into j from i
symbols.k: counts the output units (the network's last layer)
symbols.h: counts the hidden units; a unit index, not a layer count
symbols.o: a unit's output: +1 or -1 for a perceptron, between 0 and 1 for a sigmoid
symbols.delta: a unit's blame term; the gradient is minus delta times the input, so the minus stays outside
symbols.t: the target: the correct output the unit should give
symbols.eta: the learning rate: how big a step each update takes
symbols.d: one training example (as in t_d, o_d); in dσ/dx, a tiny change
symbols.bf:w: the weight vector: all of a unit's weights together, bias included
symbols.E: the error being minimised: half the squared misses added up
symbols.y: the true label of an example (+1 or -1 for a perceptron, 0 or 1 in the lab)
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.bf:x: an input vector with an extra 1 for the bias; in the search loop, the current point
symbols.partial: a partial derivative: how much the quantity changes when only the next variable changes
symbols.j: the unit a wire goes into: in w_ji, the receiving unit
symbols.n: a count: inputs to a unit, or a layer's inputs and outputs (n_in, n_out)
symbols.f: a function: ReLU's f(x), a layer's output f_i, or the function being differentiated
symbols.c: an intermediate value (a graph node) in a worked computation; in class weights, a class
symbols.Delta: the change made to the weight in one update
symbols.sigma: the sigmoid function, which squashes a total into a number between 0 and 1
symbols.a: a named quantity in an example: graph node a = e^x, or a dropout neuron's output
symbols.gamma: the margin of the perceptron's separator; in the weight penalty, the regularisation strength
symbols.p: the predicted probability of class 1 for an example (the lab's name for o)
symbols.D: the training dataset (E_D is the error over all of it); D_in is the input depth
symbols.F: the filter size: its width and height in a convolution
symbols.in: is a member of the set that follows
symbols.W: the width of the input image; in a network, a layer's weight matrix
symbols.b: a layer's bias; in the graph examples, a node b
symbols.g: the activation function (g' is its slope); in the lab, also one of a composed pair
symbols.P: zero-padding: how many border rows of zeros are added around the input
symbols.alpha: the momentum factor; for classes, the weight on class c's loss
symbols.S: the stride: how far the filter moves each step
symbols.m: the mini-batch size: how many examples go into one update
symbols.z: a unit's weighted total before squashing; in the graph rule, a child node
symbols.K: the number of filters in a convolutional layer; in pooling, one side of the J by K map
symbols.T: transpose: flips rows and columns, so w^T x is the dot product of w and x
symbols.R: the radius of the data: the length of the longest input vector
symbols.max: the largest of the values listed
symbols.nabla: the gradient: one slope per weight, pointing in the direction the error rises fastest
symbols.log: the logarithm used in the cross-entropy loss
symbols.H: the cross-entropy loss between true and predicted classes; H_out is output height
symbols.J: one side length of the feature map being pooled (a J by K map)
symbols.hat:y: the predicted probabilities, one per class, from the softmax
symbols.L: the loss (the lab's name for E)
symbols.bf:p: the search direction: which way the next step goes
symbols.lambda: the penalty strength in W1's ridge; in the lab, an eigenvalue of X^T X
symbols.w:freq: how often a class occurs in the training images
symbols.w:child: the nodes that this node feeds into directly
symbols.X: the data matrix: one row per training example
symbols.propto: is proportional to (the slide prints the class weight alpha like this)
symbols.abs: the absolute value: the size of the number, ignoring sign
symbols.w:net: a unit's weighted total of its inputs, before squashing

Neurons and the perceptron.i: counts the inputs to the unit, from the constant 1 up to n
Neurons and the perceptron.x: an input value; x_0 is the constant 1 that carries the bias

Perceptron learning.j: a second training example: one that is a misclassified negative
Perceptron learning.gamma: the margin: the gap the separator leaves around its closest point
Perceptron learning.x: an example's input values; x_i is training example i

Optimisation and gradient descent.o: the linear unit's output: w dot x, with no threshold or squashing
Optimisation and gradient descent.i: counts the unit's weights and the inputs they multiply
Optimisation and gradient descent.d: one training example, as in t_d and o_d

Multi-layer networks.W: a layer's weight matrix; W_2 W_1 x applies one layer after another

The sigmoid unit.i: counts the inputs to the unit, from the constant 1 up to n
The sigmoid unit.x: an input value, or the total fed into the sigmoid when writing the sigmoid's slope

Backpropagation.i: the unit a wire comes from: in w_ji and x_ji, the sending unit
Backpropagation.alpha: the momentum factor: how much of the previous weight change is repeated

Generalisation and capacity.gamma: the regularisation strength: how heavily large weights are charged
Generalisation and capacity.i: the unit a wire comes from, in w_ji

Neural networks for classification.t: the true class of an example, 0 or 1

Deep learning and CNNs.sigma: the softmax: turns raw scores into probabilities that add up to 1
Deep learning and CNNs.x: a unit's raw score (ReLU's input, softmax's x_j); in the dropout example, an input value
Deep learning and CNNs.y: the true class as a one-hot vector; in the dropout example, a second input
Deep learning and CNNs.i: counts the classes (in softmax and the loss)
Deep learning and CNNs.j: the class whose probability is being computed; i runs over all classes
Deep learning and CNNs.E: the expected value: the average over the random dropout patterns
Deep learning and CNNs.D: the depth of the input volume (D_in)
Deep learning and CNNs.W: the width of the input image
Deep learning and CNNs.alpha: the weight on class c's loss

Training deep networks.alpha: the weight on class c's loss: rarer classes get a larger weight
Training deep networks.y: the true class as a one-hot vector

Automatic differentiation.i: counts the layers of the network
Automatic differentiation.x: the input to the function being differentiated; f_0 = x
Automatic differentiation.e: Euler's number in e^x; also names a graph node
Automatic differentiation.W: the weight matrix of a layer; its rows are the units' weight vectors
Automatic differentiation.K: the number of layers; f_K is the final output
Automatic differentiation.z: a child node: a node this one feeds directly
Automatic differentiation.y: a node in the computation graph, not a label

Errors and inconsistencies.o: a unit's output; for a linear unit, just w dot x with no threshold

Lab exercises.w: the weight vector (the lab writes it without bold)
Lab exercises.d: a tiny change: dL/dw is the slope of the loss as w changes
Lab exercises.x: an example's inputs (x_i); in Ex 7 and 8, the variable of a function
Lab exercises.f: the function being differentiated, built from graph nodes
Lab exercises.c: the graph node c = a + b
Lab exercises.e: Euler's number in e^x; also names a graph node
Lab exercises.a: the graph node a = x squared

Backpropagation with numbers.x: an input value fed to a unit (x_1 = 1, x_2 = 0.5)
Backpropagation with numbers.i: the unit a wire comes from

Code you should recognise.y: the output of the toy function x squared, not a label
Code you should recognise.x: the variable of the toy function; in Normalize, a pixel value
Code you should recognise.delta: the lab code's error term: opposite in sign to the slides' delta

Formula sheet.i: a training example in y_i, x_i; an input or weight in w_i; in w_ji, the sending unit
Formula sheet.n: the iteration number in momentum; in n_in and n_out, a layer's input or output count
